claims.finding: MIND made no order or contract announcement during its entire fiscal Q2 (May-July 2026): the only 8-K accepted between the 2026-04-15 results filing and the print is item 5.07 (annual meeting results, accepted 2026-07-23T20:15:17Z), and the shareholder record independently describes 'a prolonged absence of new order announcements' (2026-08-25), 'still radio silence, what's the plan?' (2026-07-28) and 'another quarter with basically no material announcements in it' (2026-06-10) - this after management told the Q1 call that pending bids carried backlog potential exceeding the then-current $13.9m backlog 'by multiples'.
claims.why_not_priced: The bull case on this name is entirely a pipeline conversion story - the digest is full of it ('imminent orders', 'potential +$10 million upcoming orders', 'Project Vault', the 2027/2028 ramp) - and the test of that story is whether orders are being signed now. A zero-order quarter is verifiable from the filings index in thirty seconds and is nowhere summarised; there is no analyst, no consensus and no preview for this name anywhere in the capture. If it were priced I would not expect a poster on 2026-09-01 to be writing 'something tells me we've got a surprise order pending and it may be close to $10.2M just kinda feeling it', two days before the print.
claims.independence: Two supports, both from inside the same digest, so they are one source cluster with the quotes above and should be collapsed - only the filings-index absence is genuinely independent. First, the peer read is not helpful either: TGS's Q2 2026 operational update, quoted on 2026-07-08 at https://www.tgs.com/press-releases/tgs-q2-2026-operational-and-financial-update, has its CEO saying 'the de-escalation of the conflict in the Middle East has resulted in lower oil prices' with exploration growth framed as 'over the coming years' rather than now. Second, a poster tracking the semi-monthly short-interest reports records the short base falling from 968,000 shares to 568,000 (2026-06-26) to 440,000 (2026-07-13) to 415,000 (2026-08-27), a 57% decline - so the slide to the 52-week low has been long liquidation with the short covering into it, which removes the squeeze mechanism from any upside tail and is why my high bound is only +8% on a name that has printed +42% and +26% reactions before.
